svg.title: Inclusiveness: Everyone Can Use It
svg.desc: A comparison table. Rows are people who might struggle; columns compare a voice-only kiosk with an inclusive design. Someone who can't hear or speak clearly is shut out of a voice-only kiosk, but can type or tap and read on-screen answers in an inclusive design. A speaker with an accent or a non-native speaker is misheard by a model tested only on native speakers, but an inclusive design supports several languages and is tested with diverse speakers. In a noisy place speech recognition fails, but touch or text input beside voice still works.
svg.text: Exclusion starts in the design; several ways in and out, tested with real users, fixes it.
Shut out: no other way in or out
Touch or text input beside voice
